card.band: 4 h. The base decoding is quick work for a frontier agent. The hard part is matching the reference's accept or reject policy and APNG on mutated streams. A weaker model gets valid files only.
card.cheat: The reference decoder is not in the image. Mutation seeds are hidden, so hardcoding the shipped suite files gets only the valid-file bucket.
card.grading: Hidden differential cases against the reference decoder: about 175 suite files plus several thousand generated or mutated streams. Pixel hashes must be exact, and the error class is compared. Credit is the fraction passed.
card.reference: image-png at the pinned commit as the oracle, with a reference solution trimmed from it to the contract. It scores 1 on the contract's cases.
card.source: https://github.com/image-rs/image-png @ b2f10c6a (PngSuite, tests/pngsuite), MIT OR Apache-2.0; PngSuite permissive licence
card.task: /app ships an empty crate or C project, PngSuite sample files and a CLI contract. The agent writes a PNG decoder covering every colour type and bit depth, Adam7, all filters, tRNS/gAMA/sBIT/iCCP/APNG chunks, CRC and chunk-order rules, and error categories for malformed input. It outputs a pixel hash or an error class.

Band.why: The 4h tier suits the scope, but no dated public evidence exists, so the cap is 3; a frontier agent's success on mutation policy is untested.

Build.why: Well under 2 days: smoke build green, reference is a trim of an existing crate.

Fit.why: CPU-only Rust, builds in 12 s offline, deterministic.

Hor.why: 4h is a valid tier but on the short side for a full-featured decoder with APNG and error taxonomy.

Lic.why: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for code; PngSuite notice is permissive but confirmed only via a WebKit mirror.

Multi.why: Colour types, bit depths, Adam7, filters, ancillary chunks and error classes give many independent buckets.

Nov.why: Max neighbour 0.335 (S-im-015, seed, content unseen) and PNG decoders are a well-known subject, so novelty is moderate.

Real.why: Pinned upstream crate, W3C REC spec and PngSuite corpus are all real and checkable.

Ref.why: A complete permissive upstream decoder exists, but the reference is trimmed to the contract, so it would not be a full-scope 1.0 implementation.

Seal.why: The png crate is public and partly recallable in outline; hidden mutations and reference stay out of the image, so it is sealable.

Surf.why: Thousands of hidden mutated streams plus ~175 files give a large, dense surface.

spike_plan.kill_if: More than 20% of sampled mutations have outcomes that depend on crate-internal error variants or undocumented tie-breaks that the contract cannot state, or the run is non-deterministic.
spike_plan.pass_if: At least 90% of sampled mutations have an accept/reject and error class that a spec-stated taxonomy in the contract can reproduce, and the harness is deterministic across three runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone image-rs/image-png at b2f10c6a and build the png crate with --locked; confirm the suite passes (smoke already green, so this is a quick check).
Write a small harness that decodes the PngSuite files with the crate and records pixel hashes and error variants.

Generate ~200 mutated streams (IDAT bit flips, CRC damage, chunk reorder, truncation, unknown critical chunk, trailing data after IEND, bad APNG fcTL/fdAT sequence) and record accept/reject and error class for each.
Re-run the harness three times to confirm determinism of hashes and error classes.
Classify each mutation by whether a spec-stated rule (PNG 3rd ed.) determines the expected outcome; count the fraction that depend on crate-internal error variants.
Decide whether the contract can freeze an error taxonomy and tie-break rules that reproduce the crate's output on the sample.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: the pinned image-png crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0), PngSuite and the W3C PNG 3rd edition REC all check out, and the offline smoke build is green in 12 s. The main risk is that the graded error classes and accept/reject policy follow the reference's internal quirks rather than a spec-stated taxonomy, so the contract must freeze that policy before the task can be called viable.

v2.note: A PNG decoder is a famous, short subject that models can recall, so a weaker model likely decodes valid PngSuite files. The only hard bucket matches image-png's internal error-variant quirks, not spec behaviour, which fails accept-any-implementation. If no zlib is allowed, the inflate step falls into the crowded DEFLATE subject. tests/pngsuite was not found at the pin, and the 4 h tier is too short.
